title: Workflow authoring document
description: The authoring format for a Culture Nodes workflow (PRD §9.1, §11.1). YAML is authoring sugar; JSON is canonical, so this schema validates the JSON form. It is a *syntax and structure* gate only (PRD §11.4): graph reachability, contract compatibility, binding resolution, digest pinning, and policy checks are compiler jobs and are deliberately not attempted here. A published workflow version is immutable and content-addressed; a run pins one digest.

outcomeName.description: A declared domain outcome of a node, e.g. `completed`, `passed`, `changes_required`.

ownerRef.description: Resolved owner, e.g. `team/platform-ai`. Ownership is architecture (PRD §7): every node carries one, and authoring defaults may reduce repetition but never remove the resolved owner from the normalized JSON.

componentRef.description: Reference to a registered actor or runner, e.g. `actor://company/planner@sha256:...` or `runner://headspace/docker@sha256:...`. The compiler resolves it to an immutable digest; authoring may leave it unpinned.

pointer.description: JSON Pointer into run, node, or ledger data (PRD §11.2). Direct data movement uses pointers, never a template language.

cel.description: A CEL expression (PRD §11.2). Compiled and bounded by the compiler; not evaluated here.

schemaSource.description: A JSON Schema Draft 2020-12 contract, either referenced by path/URI or inlined.

digest.description: Set by the compiler once the referenced schema is bundled and content-addressed.

entry.description: Name of the node a run starts at. That the name exists in `nodes` is a graph-level check performed by the compiler.

limits.description: Execution limits. Optional at authoring time; the compiler expands defaults so the normalized JSON always carries bounds.

edges.description: Transitions keyed by domain outcome. May be empty only for a single-node workflow; the compiler decides reachability.

presentation.description: Presentation metadata never changes runtime semantics (PRD §9.1).

kind.description: Node kinds (PRD §9.2, §9.8). `parallel` and `join` are the split/barrier routers (issue #43): a parallel node fans out one token per eligible `<node>.split` edge, and a join node reconvenes the sibling set under its declared policy. `action.container`, `transform.wasm`, `foreach`, `subworkflow`, and `event` are named in the PRD as later work and are deliberately absent from this enum.

select.description: Decision-node output ports, each guarded by a CEL predicate (PRD §9.2, §11.2).

until.description: Wait-node resume condition: a durable time or an external signal (PRD §9.2).

presentation.description: Node presentation metadata; never changes runtime semantics.

allOf.$comment: Kind-specific minimums. Only requirements the PRD states outright are enforced; everything else is left to the compiler so authoring stays open.

joinConfig.description: A join node's barrier policy (PRD §9.8, issue #43). The sibling set the barrier counts against is discovered at split time (token_groups.cardinality), never declared here. `first_success` is deliberately not in this enum: domain outcomes carry no success/failure typing (PRD §3.4), so "first success" has no honest meaning yet — a recorded PRD deviation, see the parallel-tokens design §10.

quorum.description: Required iff policy is `quorum` (a compiler check); how many arrivals fire the barrier.

nodeContract.description: Node contract (PRD §9.3): input schema, one output schema per domain outcome, and an error schema. JSON Schema is a validation language, not a decidable subtyping system — runtime validation stays mandatory even when the compiler proves edge compatibility.

inputBinding.description: Either a whole-value move (`from`) or named field bindings, each a JSON Pointer (PRD §11.2).

codeOperation.description: Authoring shape of a code node's operation. The compiler lowers this to the runner-agnostic operation contract in ../runner/operation.schema.json. A code node describes an operation; a runner executes it — no shell, script, or Docker socket ever runs in a control-plane process (PRD §9.2).

argv.description: An argument array, never a shell string.

requiresShell.description: Declared explicitly when a shell is genuinely required, so policy can reject it.

preRunHook.description: A code operation the engine/worker executes through the runner boundary BEFORE an agent node's actor is dispatched (plan task t14, spec claim c37). The operation is the same authoring shape a code node declares (PRD §9.2, §13.7): no shell, script, or Docker socket ever runs in a control-plane process. Failure semantics (honesty condition h32) are fixed, not authored: a pre-run hook that fails fails the attempt before agent dispatch as a technical failure, retryable per the node's own retry policy, and the agent is never invoked.

postRunHook.description: A code operation the engine/worker executes through the runner boundary AFTER an agent node's actor returns (plan task t14, spec claim c37). `on_failure` is required: a post-run check failure must map to a declared domain outcome of the node or to an assurance rejection, never to silence (honesty condition h32).

hookOnFailure.description: What a failing post-run hook (an operation that ran and exited nonzero) routes to: a domain outcome the node declares, so a workflow can steer a failed check down its own edge, or an explicit assurance rejection recorded against the agent's result while the agent's own domain outcome still stands.

ledgerDelta.description: The node's ledger delta contract (PRD §10.7): the projection it may read, and the record types it may propose or observe. Authority is still enforced by the ledger runtime at append time — declaring `observe` does not grant an agent the right to issue observed evidence.

projectionName.description: Standard ledger projections (PRD §10.9). Domain projections may be registered later; this enum is intentionally closed for now so typos fail loudly.

acceptance.description: Mechanical acceptance checks (PRD §10.10). Check payloads stay open until the check registry lands with the compiler; only `kind` is required. `enforce` declares what a failed check does to routing; omitting it means `observe`.

enforce.description: Policy for a failed acceptance check (issue #37). `observe` — the default when the field is omitted, and today's behavior — records the verdict as a derived record without touching routing. `route_technical` fails the attempt with the engine's `contract_rejected` technical status. `route_outcome:<name>` follows the graph edge of a domain outcome the node itself declares; the compiler rejects a name the node's contract does not declare.

edge.description: A transition into a node, sourced either from another node's declared domain outcome (`from`) or from a named external event (`onEvent`). Exactly one of the two. `changes_required` is an outcome that follows an edge, never an engine failure (PRD §3.4).

onEvent.description: An event name (issue #43): when a signal event of this name is delivered to a run of this workflow, a token is created at `to` and the node runs. Several edges may name one event — one delivery then creates one token per matching edge, which is how an event splits. Routes are multi-fire and bounded by spec.limits (§9.7); an event edge may not target an `end` node.

when.description: Optional CEL guard on the transition. An `onEvent` edge's guard additionally sees `event` ({name, payload, emitter}).
